title: Chapter 148: Nine Patients, Ten Rooms
html:
Chen Ge pushed open the bathroom door. A black cloth covered the mirror on the wall, and the cubicle door remained sealed.

Visitors only enter during the day, while the blood door appears only at midnight.

Under normal circumstances, the two should never cross paths—unless someone sneaks into the Haunted House at night and opens the cubicle by accident, as Zhang Peng did.

Chen Ge removed the black cloth and stood before the mirror.

He knew nothing about the blood-red world beyond it. He did not even understand why the door appeared, let alone how to destroy it.

My parents said the door at the Third Sick Hall had opened again, which means it was once closed. Perhaps the hospital contains a clue to sealing it. The door there may even be connected to the one in this mirror. That makes the Trial Mission even more important.

Chen Ge waited until midnight. As the second hand crossed twelve, the blood door appeared in the mirror precisely on time. During its brief minute of existence, strange noises spilled from behind the cubicle. There seemed to be more things crowding around the door than before.

Perhaps when I return from the Third Sick Hall, I can close this door for good.

Unable to sleep, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room and began listing everything he needed for tomorrow’s livestream. A cleaver steeped in years of blood, a live rooster, salt…

He worked until 1:50 a.m., but sleep remained elusive. Every few minutes, he checked his watch as an inexplicable unease spread through him.

This still isn’t safe enough. A Three-Star Trial Mission should be several times harder than the Two-Star Mu Yang High School, and I’m going in alone. I need to prepare more thoroughly.While taking stock of everything he owned, his phone suddenly rang. Who’s calling me at two in the morning?

One glance at the caller ID, and Chen Ge answered at once. “Doctor Gao? Is something wrong?”

“I’m sorry to disturb you so late,” Doctor Gao said politely before coming straight to the point. “I obtained Wang Shenglong’s medical history from his father. When I cross-referenced it against the records of one of our own patients, I discovered something strange.”

“What did you find?” Chen Ge sat straighter. If Doctor Gao was calling at this hour, it had to be serious.

“Wang Shenglong is more dangerous than he appears. When he was very young, he was involved in a murder.”

“A murder?” Chen Ge could hardly believe the chubby child had been involved in anything so sinister.

“Hear me out. The case is complicated.” Typing sounded over the phone. “Wang Shenglong first received treatment at six years old. The facility was called the Jiujiang Third Psychological Convalescence Center, a private institution far outside the city. It closed five or six years ago.”

“Wang Hailong mentioned that hospital. His family was poor at the time, and it stood near their old home, so they admitted Shenglong there. But what does that have to do with the murder?”

“When he was first admitted, six-year-old Wang Shenglong displayed violent mood swings. He would lose control and attack both doctors and family members.”

“However unruly he was, a six-year-old couldn’t seriously hurt an adult, could he?”

“That’s what I assumed, but according to the files, he once flew into a frenzy and bit off the finger of another patient in his room. I have a photograph.” Doctor Gao sent it over without censoring the gruesome details. It was part of Wang Shenglong’s patient file, which classified him as extremely dangerous and recommended strict isolation.

“And that was only the beginning. For the other patients’ safety, the doctors moved six-year-old Wang Shenglong into the third sealed building. From there, matters grew worse.” Doctor Gao selected several pages that would not violate patient confidentiality and sent them to Chen Ge. “During Shenglong’s second month in the isolation ward, a nurse on duty was brutally murdered. The police investigation concluded that there had been more than one killer. It appeared that every patient in the third hall had cooperated in the murder.”

“The patients worked together to kill a nurse?” Doctor Gao was sharing inside information about the Third Sick Hall, and Chen Ge listened intently. “Can you tell me anything else about the case?”

“That’s everything I have. I’m a doctor, not a police officer.”

“Then can you find more information about the other patients in the Third Sick Hall?” Chen Ge wanted to learn everything he could about the place.

“Why would you want to know about that?”

“I’m merely curious. Don’t worry—I won’t share the information with anyone.” Only after several more assurances did Doctor Gao agree.

“The Third Sick Hall had ten rooms but only nine patients. Each had been deemed extremely dangerous and isolated for specialized treatment.

“Room 1 held Wang Shenglong. He was diagnosed with Angelman syndrome, sometimes called Happy Puppet syndrome. His symptoms included constant smiling, seizures, loss of speech, and developmental disability. He was the youngest patient in the Third Sick Hall and considered the least dangerous.

“Room 2 held a woman, but her name has been blacked out. There is no photograph; all I found was an old patient list. She suffered from severe depression caused by Dorian Gray syndrome. She was obsessed with her appearance, dependent on makeup, and unable to accept natural aging. She had undergone numerous cosmetic procedures. The condition is not uncommon among female celebrities.

“Room 3 was supposedly empty. I can’t determine whether it ever housed a patient.”

Chen Ge immediately recalled the note his parents had left, which specifically mentioned Room 3 of the Third Sick Hall. “No record doesn’t mean there was no patient.”

“You may be right, but the rooms were assigned by danger level. Even if Room 3 was occupied, its patient could not have been considered especially dangerous. It may simply have been a clerical error.” Doctor Gao paused for a sip of water before continuing.

“The patient in Room 4 developed phantom limb syndrome after losing an arm in an accident. Even after the amputation, he remained convinced the arm was attached and claimed he could feel pain and changes in temperature through it.”
